advances: Ordinary strict triangle cuts in the specified canonical normalization. The determinant retains the coarea scale in these coordinates.

proof:
In [5f923438468803ac](../facts/5f923438468803ac.md), the hypotheses are precisely the present strict corner cuts with ordinary cap area and coarea. Its proof identifies $H=2M$ as the sum of the three positive margins, $u_i=v_i\cdot(P_i-P_{i+1})/H$ and $v_i\cdot(P_i-P_{i+2})/H=1-u_{i+1}$, and gives $f_i^2=4u_i(1-u_{i+1})$ with $0<u_i<1$. Hence $f_1f_2f_3=8\sqrt{PR}$. In the canonical coordinates, the normalized vectors $(P_1-P_2)/H$ and $(P_1-P_3)/H$ are $(u_1,-(1-u_3))$ and $(1-u_2,u_2+u_3-1)$, respectively. Their determinant is $1-\sum_i u_i+\sum_{i<j}u_i u_j=P+R>0$. The absolute determinant equals $2k/H^2$, yielding the first identity and then the third.

By the definition of the positive $f_i$, the inequality $k/M^2\ge\tfrac12\prod_i f_i$ rearranges to $M\prod_i\sigma_i\ge4\sqrt{kQ_1Q_2Q_3}$. The third identity says equality is equivalent to $P=R$. In the same coordinates the cubic deficit is $4-4\sum_i u_i(1-u_{i+1})-8\sqrt{PR}=4(\sqrt P-\sqrt R)^2$, by expanding $P+R$. This gives the equality condition.

source_sections.locator: (1)–(2), strict triangle scale identity and equality

statement:
Use the canonical balanced normals $(1,0),(0,1),(-1,-1)$ and a marked interior point in a nondegenerate triangle with strict distinct-vertex incidence. Let $k,Q_i,\sigma_i$ be respectively the area, cap areas and chord lengths divided by the respective normal lengths. Set $M=\sum_iQ_i/\sigma_i$, $H=2M$, $f_i=2\sqrt{kQ_i}/(\sigma_iM)$ and $u_i=v_i\cdot(P_i-P_{i+1})/H$ cyclically for the matched vertices $P_i$. Put $P=\prod_i u_i$, $R=\prod_i(1-u_i)$. Then
$$
2k/H^2=P+R,\qquad \prod_i f_i=8\sqrt{PR},\qquad
k/M^2-\tfrac12\prod_i f_i=2(\sqrt P-\sqrt R)^2.
$$
In particular $M\prod_i\sigma_i\ge4\sqrt{kQ_1Q_2Q_3}$, with equality exactly when $\sum_i f_i^2+\prod_i f_i=4$.
title: Exact coarea scale identity for strict ordinary triangle cuts
